title: using Astra to optimize entire game until it looks like reference image(s)
author: invocation02
selftext:
context: i'm making a killing-floor 2 style game, but Terminator theme with AI. Astra was able to whip up a playable game in one level in the first day, but the quality of all the assets were very bad. everything is low poly, some of the weapon assets incoherent with floating parts, etc. i've had some success getting astra to improve assets in isolation in blender. astra is pretty shit at open ended generation, but if you give a concrete 3d asset or image reference its able to converge towards it by using the pixel-diff against reference as the error signal. the problem with this approach is poor consistency - all the references must share consistent style, which is hard to do when sourcing free assets online. 

i thought image gen models might be able to solve this - they can generate images containing many game assets in consistent Terminator style. my approach was to take many screenshots of the game level from the player's POV, and restyle the screenshots using an image gen model to get the reference image. then ask astra to optimize everything in the game until error between new screenshots and reference image is zero.

its been running for several hours and above is the result - left column screenshot from unoptimized game, middle column target image generated by gpt-image-2, right column screenshot from the latest astra-optimized game. wondering if anyone tried this and had good results, or know a better method.

comments.author: Original-League-6094
comments.body: I mean, its getting there. Are you doing it within a game engine, or is it building its own?

replies.author: invocation02
replies.body: yeah, i'm doing it in a threejs based browser game engine called kite3d [https://github.com/blitzdotdev/kite3d](https://github.com/blitzdotdev/kite3d) that i'm developing. that's also what i'm realizing so far, all the viral 3D demos i've seen on X of Astra are probably fake.

replies.author: TopTippityTop
replies.body: Not the most optimized, let's just say

replies.author: Interesting-Bee-113
replies.body:
Not yet. This is just the hero asset.

All the internals are in there too. Engine, headers, exhaust, turbos, radiators and cooling hoses, the entire suspension assembly for the front and rear. The steering assembly for the front. The interior cabin.

replies.author: invocation02
replies.body: What guidance did you give the model? What references did it have access to?

replies.author: Interesting-Bee-113
replies.body:
2D concept sheets for detail.

And a 3D model generated with Meshy that I really wasn't happy with for shape and geometry.

It still took a lot of steering and correcting by mostly taking screenshots and marking them up in paint.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: nice, I used mine on trying a human model with a reference but it didn't quite get to where I was hoping. did you have one reference or many?

replies.author: Interesting-Bee-113
replies.body:
Many references

One 3D model from Meshy

And a collection of concept sheets.

And most of the good corrections landed after I meticulously marked up what I was trying to articulate on screen shots in paint instead of flailing with words at the agent.

It still took like 12 hours and nearly my entire weekly codex budget.
